messages:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: p1 page for GPU-POOL-CAPACITY (auto-escalation) — queue depth > 10k, 90th pct latency spiking. Impact: inference jobs throttled. Paging on-call for incidents. :rotating_light:

maria: I'm on call. joining. seeing alerts for cluster autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes. logs show "No matching node group for labels" and launch template mismatch errors.

sam: Trying to pull kubectl logs now, hold on.

sam: (log snippet)
```
I0501 12:03:21 autoscaler.go:123] scale-up predicate failed: no node groups match selector
E0501 12:04:02 launchtemplate.go:45] LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch: requested version 2024-07-15 not found in nodegroup gpu-pool-v2
```

maria: Ok so autoscaler is rejecting because the ASG's launch template version tag doesn't match selector the autoscaler expects. That plus taint/labels changed after the recent runtime rollout.

dean: Also seeing high spot termination rates in the affected AZs — several scaling attempts ended with nodes failing to join due to AMI boot errors.

jess: Customer-facing metric: embedding queue length upstream is 12k, downstream latency > 8s (norm 0.6s). Some customers seeing 429s. Not wide data loss but throttling.

maria: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) create temporary emergency nodegroup with compatible LT/AMI and correct labels; 2) increase desired capacity on that group; 3) patch autoscaler nodeGroupSelector to include emergency group; 4) drain and reprovision failed nodes. Doing 1 and 2 now.

sam: Command I'm running to create node group (eksctl-like):
```
eksctl create nodegroup --cluster redwood-prod --name gpu-emergency-1 --node-type p4d.24xlarge --ami ami-0c12345 --labels role=gpu,model=rt-v1 --taints nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule --nodes 3 --nodes-min 3 --nodes-max 20
```

infra-bot: Cloud: Created ASG gpu-emergency-1 (id: asg-0a1b2c3d). Launch template ami=ami-0c12345, lt-version=1.

maria: Patching cluster-autoscaler configmap to accept new nodegroup selector so it can scale it up automatically. Patch applied.

sam: Autoscaler logs now: "Found node group: gpu-emergency-1, scaling up to 8". New instances launching.

dean: Instances are coming up but kubelet shows TLS boot error on a couple, probably missing cloud-init step. I'll try remote exec to grab journalctl.

sam: Attaching the set of commands we used to speed-join nodes (for runbook):
```
# bootstrap fix: re-run cloud-init
ssh ec2-user@<ip> 'sudo cloud-init status --wait || sudo cloud-init single --name cc_bootstrap'
kubectl label node <node> role=gpu model=rt-v1
kubectl taint nodes <node> nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule-
```

jess: Observability — traffic is backfilling into workers. Queue depth dropping: 12k -> 6k in 10m after emergency group reached 6 nodes. Latency down to ~2s, error rate falling.

maria: Next step: reconcile launch template versions. There's a mismatch between the autoscaler's node-group spec (expects lt-version 3) and the ASG (version 1). Ops will create LT v3 and update ASG. Doing that now but it's higher risk.

dean: Noting: the original rollout changed node label semantics from "gpu-role" to "role=gpu" which made the autoscaler selectors miss nodegroups. We'll capture that in the postmortem.

sam: Manual scale to accelerate recovery: asg set-desired-capacity gpu-emergency-1 12 --honor-cooldown false

infra-bot: ASG asg-0a1b2c3d desired=12 instances launching.

maria: Coordinating customer comms: Jess, can you flag top 10 affected accounts and draft a brief? Emphasize throttling and mitigation in progress.

jess: On it. Drafting message: "We're experiencing increased inference latency and reduced throughput due to GPU node provisioning issues. We've provisioned emergency capacity and expect full recovery in ~30-45m. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a root cause postmortem."

sam: Autoscaler now steadily adding nodes from emergency group. Metrics show GPU utilization per pod back to expected range. Queue at 1.1k and trending down.

maria: Mitigation status: emergency nodegroup healthy, autoscaler selectors patched, launch template v3 created and scheduled for ASG update. Rolling update window set to avoid mass reboot.

dean: Quick note about permissions: the autoscaler IAM role couldn't describe launch templates because the role's policy was scoped to resource arn:aws:ec2:::launch-template/lt-prod-* and new LT had different name. Fixing policy to allow explicit LT id.

sam: After IAM policy change, autoscaler logs show it discovered LT v3 and reconciled nodegroup definitions. Scaling resumed normally.

pagerduty-bot: Incident severity reduced to P2 — partial service degradation mitigated.

maria: We'll keep this thread open. Action items for post-incident: (1) revert or standardize node label changes in runtime rollout, (2) ensure LT versioning and autoscaler selectors are part of rollout checklist, (3) expand autoscaler's IAM test coverage to include DescribeLaunchTemplate, (4) add a runbook step to create emergency nodegroups.

jess: Customer comms sent to affected top accounts. No escalations yet.

maria: last checks: queue 300, latency 0.8s. Marking as mitigated. I'll start an incident doc. Recommend a small on-call follow-up meeting in 1hr to hand off the postmortem timeline. :white_check_mark:
